constraints.text: "We never know what's past the next tree line, over the next rise, or around the next corner unless we see it for ourselves."
constraints.reading: The hiding spot is concealed just beyond an edge of woods (a tree line), implying the spot sits where forest meets open ground or where one band of trees ends.
The spot lies just over the top of a low hill or rise - on the far side of a crest, out of sight from the near approach. Stand at a small summit/ridge and look down the opposite slope.
The spot is around a bend - a turn in a trail, a road, or a terrain feature (rock outcrop, ridge spur) that hides it from a straight-line view. Follow the path past the curve.

constraints.text: "the box sits just out of normal sightline at a spot most people walk past" (Research Findings)
constraints.reading: Hiding spot is hidden from the casual sightline of someone at a road, overlook, or trailhead - not at the obvious viewpoint or parking area, but a short distance beyond where the view 'breaks'.

constraints.text: "in mountaineering 'tree line' means timberline (the elevation above which trees stop growing); if read that strongly it would point to a high-elevation, near-summit setting" (Research Findings)
constraints.reading: Speculative alternate reading: 'past the next tree line' could mean above timberline - a high, near-summit setting where trees thin out. Flagged speculative even in source.

constraints.text: "Even the watchful purple hills / That hold the lake" (Earhart poem 'From an Airplane')
constraints.reading: Spatial image of hills cradling/encircling a body of water - the spot may be on a hillside or slope overlooking a lake, with high ground wrapping around the water. 'Hold the lake' = ringed/embraced by hills.
Hills described as purple - a distant/atmospheric color cast (purple haze of ridgelines at dusk). Suggests viewing distant hills, possibly from elevation.

constraints.text: "Could not see so well as I / The stain of evening / Creeping from its heart"
constraints.reading: Implies a high, commanding vantage with a long downward view ('see so well') - looking out over a lake/valley as evening shadow spreads. The spot may be a high overlook.

constraints.text: "Nor the round, yellow eyes of the hamlet / Growing filmy with mists"
constraints.reading: 'Round, yellow eyes' = round glowing lights of a small village seen from above/afar; 'filmy with mists' suggests a misty valley or low-lying fog. The viewpoint sits above a hamlet, looking down through mist.

constraints.text: "the green backdrop of Londonderry" / treasure photo taken against a green field (provenance)
constraints.reading: The defining treasure image is set against a green open field/pasture with the subject standing in the open - a grassy clearing rather than dense forest or rock.

constraints.text: Treasure photo: Earhart "standing on/beside her Lockheed Vega 5B" in a flat open pasture
constraints.reading: Imagery of a figure standing upright in/on a flat open ground beside a large object - echoes a level clearing or flat where one would stand next to a prominent feature.

constraints.text: Birthplace described as "on a bluff over the Missouri River" / "on a hillside overlooking Warnock Lake" with a "hilltop viewing deck" (Places, raw facts)
constraints.reading: Recurring spatial motif in the chapter's geography: high ground (bluff/hillside/hilltop) positioned directly above and overlooking water - a raised vantage point over a lake or river.

constraints.text: "a plaque at Diamond Head Lookout" and Earhart Peak (~11,974 ft summit) as named features (Places, raw facts)
constraints.reading: Associated landmarks are lookouts and peaks - reinforces a high overlook / summit-vantage character for the spot, a place with a commanding view.

constraints.text: "By 1966 he built a studio/gallery on a rocky knoll" (Loloma, Research Findings, raw fact)
constraints.reading: Spatial image of a small rocky knoll (a low rocky rise/hillock) as a chosen high spot - a candidate microfeature: a rocky knob or outcrop.

constraints.text: "the International Forest of Friendship (a living memorial with trees from all 50 states)" (Places, raw fact)
constraints.reading: Spatial motif of a stand/grove of distinctive trees as a marker - the spot may be associated with a notable cluster or line of trees (reinforces the 'tree line' edge imagery).
